title: Hotel refused in Providence with Benny Goodman; Charlie Barnett and Boyd Raeburn
summary: Young, Teddy Wilson and Slam Stewart were refused a hotel room; Goodman did not fight it, unlike Barnett and Raeburn.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Barnett had a lot of problems over -- when we used to play with Barnett. We didn't go way down South. We'd be in places like West Virginia, you know. And he'd have a problem. I remember once with Benny Goodman, it was Teddy, Slam and myself, we had a problem in Providence in a hotel.
Well, they didn't want us. So, Teddy approached Benny. He says -- he said, we have a problem here. We can't get a room in the hotel. He said, we though you made

a reservation. Benny said -- then he says they don't want to let us have a room. So, Benny didn't go to the front for this, you know. He said you know I have problems too. I can't belong to this Jewish club, this club or that one because I'm Jewish.
So, we told him we was going back to New York. We told him thanks very much but we were going -- we didn't have to go through that. Then he got something done about it when we told him that.
No, he went and got somebody else to do something about it.
That's what I wondered. I mean I've heard so many Benny Goodman stories.

Yeah, he didn't. But I don't know. He's strange anyway, you know. You got a strange person, you know. But he wouldn't battle those things out. But that's one thing I can say about Charlie. He would fight, man. He would. And so would Boyd Raeburn. I played with Boyd Raeburn's band, you know. And Boyd was a beautiful cat -- did you ever know him?
No, I never did. I know he had a great band but --
He was a beautiful cat, man. He'd fight. You know, he would -- he'd say, well, they don't stay here, none of us stay here, you know. That was his way, you know.

But I guess everybody wasn't like that, you know. I liked Benny, you know, but I don't think Benny would go too far for nobody. Not only us but nobody else, you know. He didn't think like that. He just thought clarinet and that was it, you know.
Great, great player. The guy's a great player but that's what he -- the way he thought was strictly clarinet. He didn't let anything else bother him. Clarinet was it, man, you know.
